title: What must be added to reach the bigger number?
description: A child has ten rupees and the sister has six, and the gap between them is the money still to be added. Three take away questions are then turned into missing number questions in the same way. Keeko's doubt is that the missing number is found by adding the two numbers shown.
teaching_notes: One idea: take away can be read as finding the missing number that must be added to the smaller number to reach the bigger one. Watch for students who add the two given numbers instead of finding the gap between them.

video_script.why: The child reads take away as finding the missing number to be added, the idea that later gives the button press in the lift.
video_script.substitution: Turn each take away into a missing number sum: the small number plus what makes the big number.
video_script.anchor: the book's two sisters with ten rupees and six rupees, then three take away questions
video_script.wrong_move: adds the two numbers given instead of finding the gap between them
video_script.payoff_line: Take away means finding the missing number to be added.
maths_rules: slip: 5 + 15 = 20 adds the two given numbers, but 5 + 20 = 25, not 15
video_script.design: One idea: take away is a missing number to be added. The book's two sisters open the video, then three questions on one board.

beats.on_screen: title card From your book; a child holding 10 rupees and the sister holding 6 rupees

marks.sis: the child with ten rupees and the sister with six rupees appear
marks.ask: a question mark floats between the two amounts

narration: <bookmark mark='scene'/>This is a question from your book about subtraction.
<bookmark mark='sis'/>A child has ten rupees, and the sister has only six rupees.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>How much more money must the sister get to have the same amount?

beats.on_screen: the question stays on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: 6 + ? = 10 with the missing 4 filled in; 10 - 6 = 4 written beside it

marks.gap: 6 + ? = 10 appears and the missing 4 fills in

narration: <bookmark mark='gap'/>Six plus the missing amount must make ten, and that missing amount is four.
<bookmark mark='same'/>Ten take away six asks for that very same missing number.

marks.given: the three take away questions are written

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, three questions. Fifteen take away five, a hundred take away ten, and seventy four take away thirty four.

beats.on_screen: To find: each answer as a missing number to be added

marks.find: the words missing number to be added are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find each answer as the missing number to be added.

marks.first: 15 - 5 turns into 5 + ? = 15 and the missing 10 fills in

narration: <bookmark mark='first'/>Step one, fifteen take away five becomes five plus a missing number equals fifteen.
Five and ten make fifteen, so the missing number is ten.

marks.second: 100 - 10 turns into 10 + ? = 100 and the missing 90 fills in

narration: <bookmark mark='second'/>Step two, a hundred take away ten becomes ten plus a missing number equals a hundred.
Ten and ninety make a hundred, so the missing number is ninety.

marks.gapline: a gap is drawn from 34 up to 74

narration: <bookmark mark='third'/>Step three, seventy four take away thirty four becomes thirty four plus a missing number equals seventy four.
<bookmark mark='gapline'/>We look for the gap that climbs from thirty four up to seventy four.

beats.on_screen: 34 + 40 = 74; answers 10, 90, 40; Take away means finding the missing number to be added

marks.gap: the gap is filled with 40 and 34 + 40 = 74 is written
marks.pay: the line take away means finding the missing number to be added glows
marks.all: the three answers 10, 90 and 40 are boxed

narration: <bookmark mark='gap'/>The missing number is forty, because thirty four and forty make seventy four.
<bookmark mark='pay'/>Take away means finding the missing number to be added.
<bookmark mark='all'/>The three answers are ten, ninety and forty.
<bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: 5 + 20 = 25 crossed out next to 5 + ? = 15, and the gap from 5 to 15 marked as 10

marks.gap: the gap from 5 to 15 lights up as 10

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks the missing number is twenty, because five and fifteen make twenty.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>But five plus twenty makes twenty five, and that is not fifteen.
<bookmark mark='gap'/>The missing number is the gap between the two numbers, so it is ten.
